items.prompt: White has just played Qc8+, a check. It is Black's move. How many legal replies does Black have? Count the moves that take the checking queen, block the line and move the king.

claims.statement: Black is in check.
Black has exactly two legal moves: the king to h5 and the f-pawn to f5.

hints: A check can be answered in three ways: take the checking piece, put a piece in its way, or move the king.
Try each of the three ways in turn. Which of them exist in this position?
No black piece can take the queen. The king has one square, and one pawn can block.
items.explain: Black has exactly two legal replies: the king steps to h5, or the f-pawn blocks on f5. To call Qc8+ a mate in two, White needs a mating move after each of them.

items.prompt: Black answered Qc8+ with Kh5. White to move. Find the checkmate.

claims.statement: Qxh3 is checkmate.
Qxh3 is a legal move.

hints: The queen on c8 already stands on a long diagonal.
Which black piece or pawn on that diagonal can the queen capture with check?
The queen takes the pawn on h3.
items.explain: Qxh3 is checkmate: the queen gives check along the h-file and the king has no move. A different reply needs a different mating move, so each reply has to be checked on its own.

items.prompt: White to move. Rb8+ forces mate in two here. Suppose White tries the other check, Qh7+, instead. Does Qh7+ force mate in two? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Qh7+ is a legal move.
After Qh7+ the black king attacks the queen on h7.
No white piece defends the queen on h7.
Qh7+ is far worse than Rb8+ (the engine finds no mate after it, depth 16).
After Rb8+ the black king on g8 has no legal move.

hints: After a check, one reply is to take the checking piece. Can Black do that here?
Which black piece attacks h7, and does any white piece defend h7?
The king stands next to h7 and nothing defends the queen.
items.explain: No. After Qh7+ the king can simply take the queen: it attacks h7 and nothing defends it. After Rb8+ the king has no legal move at all, which is why that check is the strong one.

items.prompt: White to move. Does White have a forced mate in two?

answer.class: No, there is no forced mate in two

claims.statement: The engine shows no mate here and rates the position between three pawns worse and one pawn better for White (depth 16).
The check Re8+ is at least three pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
After Re8+ the rook on d8 attacks e8.
After Re8+ the rook on e8 is loose: attacked and not defended.
After Ne7+ the knight on e7 is attacked twice (rook and knight).

hints: List every check White has. For each check, list the replies.
Look at the rook on d8 and at the squares e8 and e7.
Re8+ can be taken by the rook on d8, and Ne7+ can be taken by the rook or the knight.
items.explain: White has two checks and neither works: Re8+ is taken by the rook, and Ne7+ is taken by the rook or the knight. The engine finds no forced mate and rates the position close to level, so the answer is "no forced mate in two".
options: Yes, there is a forced mate in two
No, there is no forced mate in two

items.prompt: White to move. There is a forced mate in two, and the first move is not a check. Find it.

claims.statement: Nxd7 forces checkmate in two.
Nxd7 is the engine's best move (depth 16).
Nxd7 is not a check: no white piece attacks the king's square afterwards.
After Nxd7 the enemy king has 0 legal moves.
Before Nxd7 no black piece covers b6, the square of the mating move.

hints: No check works here, so look for a quiet first move. Count the squares the enemy king can use.
Which move makes a mating threat that the defender cannot meet with a check or a capture?
The first move is made by the knight on c5.
items.explain: Nxd7 is not a check, but it takes the rook and leaves the black king with no legal move, and it threatens Nb6#. The engine confirms that every reply allows mate next move.

feedback_by_move.c5a4: Na4 also threatens Nb6#, but Black has the counter-check Rxc7+ (see the next exercise).

items.prompt: White to move. Nxd7 forces mate in two. Suppose White plays Na4 instead. It also threatens Nb6#. Does Na4 force mate in two? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Na4 is a legal move.
After Na4 Rxc7+ the black rook attacks the white king on c6: it is check.
After Na4 Rxc7+ the rook on c7 is defended once, by the black king.
Na4 is far worse than Nxd7 (at least ten pawns, depth 16).

hints: After White's move, ask what Black can do with a check of its own.
Which black piece can give check on c6, and is that piece safe from capture?
The rook on d7 can take the pawn on c7 with check, and the king defends c7.
items.explain: No. After Na4 Black has the counter-check Rxc7+. The rook is defended by the king, so White cannot take it, and the threat of Nb6# is gone. Nxd7 works because it takes that rook away.

claims.statement: Nxd7 is a legal move.

hints: The mating move was Nb6. Which black piece could take a knight on b6?
Look at the a-pawn. Which squares does a pawn on a7 attack?
A pawn on a7 attacks b6, so Nb6 could simply be captured.
items.explain: No. The pawn on a7 covers b6, so after Nxd7 the threat Nb6# can be met by axb6. One extra defender on the key square removes the mate; the engine finds no forced mate and rates Black better.
